newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Times groups' Q2 oper profit rise.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Times groups' Q2 oper profit rise.

text.p: New York Times Co said Thursday it had during the second quarter operating profits in its newspaper group of $119.4 million, $11.9 milllion in its broadcast group and $9.2 million in its magazine group.
For the second quarter of 1996, the company had operating profits of $86.6 million in its newspaper group, $8.2 million in its broadcast group and $6.5 million in its magazine group.
The company said a 10 percent increase in the newspaper group's revenues was primarily the result of higher advertising revenues from higher rates and volume.
It said continued strength in classified and national advertising was also a significant factor.

The company also said revenue and operating profit increases at the broadcasting group were principally the result of acquisition of two NBC affiliates which were acquired in July 1996, as well as stronger advertising revenues at WTKR-TV, Norfolk, Virginia.
The two new stations contributed $3.6 million of operating profit in the quarter.

In addition, the company said the magazine group's operating profit increase was primarily the result of higher advertising revenues from higher ad volume at Golf Co, partially offset by increased losses associated with new ventures.
New York Times Co reported earnings per share of $0.85 compared to $0.48 for the same period a year ago.
